column1: # The `-O` harness on the Apple M4 (MacBook Air, Mac16,12, macOS 26.6.2) that
# stands in for the M3 from 2026-10-21. The M3's `-O` points are mined from
# each ref's BENCHMARKS.md; these are the M4's, and gen-dashboard draws them
# as an optbench_m4 block beside the M3's, never joined to them (see the
# EIGHTH SITTING in bench-backfill.tsv for why the two machines' milliseconds
# unchanged from v5.3.0 to v5.5.0), driven by a 5.4.1-193-g403a7e70 build:
# the v5.3.0 and v5.5.0 rakupp-macos-universal.tar.gz, sha256 verified, arm64
# slice, two passes each in the order v5.3.0, v5.5.0, v5.5.0, v5.3.0, every
# program checked four ways before it was timed; the harness's best of 5 a
# pass, then the minimum across the passes. Rakudo is the 2026.09 homebrew
# arm64 bottle, the same build as the kernels' Rakudo. bigmul is timed by the
# harness but not charted, as on the M3.
# v5.3.0 is the bridge: the M3's last `-O` point. On it the M4 takes
# 0.84-0.89x of the M3's time. Against it, v5.5.0 runs plain --exe nummath
# and arrayidx 6-8% slower in both modes.
# SECOND SITTING, 2026-11-11, the same M4 (macOS 26.6.2 / Darwin 25.6.0, load
# average 2.2-3.5 throughout). The rows of v5.4.0, v5.4.1 and v5.6.0 to v5.7.0
# below; v5.3.0 and v5.5.0 keep their 2026-10-22 rows. Each tag's released
# rakupp-macos-universal.tar.gz, sha256 verified, arm64 slice, driven by a
# 8c195e04); programs unchanged since v5.3.0. Two passes, ascending then
# descending, minimum of the two. Rakudo, the same 2026.09 bottle, was timed
# beside v5.7.0 only and is the value on every row of this sitting. The
# sitting re-ran v5.3.0 and v5.5.0 too, as a bridge: sieve -O 19.0 and 22.0 ms
# against 19.5 and 21.7, nummath --exe 182.1 and 14.5 against 184.6 and 14.8.
# Peak RSS from the same runs is in memory-m4.tsv.
